findings.evidence: “Record its printed path; like the entrypoint, write it literally” repeats the shell-call persistence reminder at lines 49–50.
findings.fix: Put one shared note beside entrypoint resolution for both ENTRYPOINT and WORK. Keep the scratch-directory and inventory-placement rules at step 1, and record the duplicate wording as consolidated.

findings.evidence: “Set up a cross-AI execution runner” describes setup, but the only explicit boundary is with gsd-settings/gsd-config; the description does not distinguish configuring the runner from dispatching a lane through an existing runner.
findings.fix: Use when a project needs a quick GSD setup or a migration from v1 to v2: recommend models per tier, wire installed skills to GSD agents, and preview and apply changes to `.planning/config.json`, including cross-AI plan review and execution hooks. Also use to render or upgrade `cross-ai.mjs`, run `ensure-runner`, or merge `cross-ai.mjs.new`. Use `gsd-settings` or `gsd-config` for advanced settings and integrations, and `ai-kit-cross-ai` to dispatch a lane or handle its runtime failure.

findings.evidence: “The rendered runner (`cross-ai.mjs`) has its own” introduces a dispatch-status table in the always-loaded prerequisites, though the ordinary configuration flow never dispatches a model call.
findings.fix: Move the runner exit/status mapping to `references/runner.md` under its existing non-ok dispatch trigger. Keep the curated CLI's exit table and the instruction to read `AIKIT-XAI status=` rather than guessing from the runner's numeric exit.

findings.evidence: “Apply only after the user answers” gates writes on approval but does not say what to do if the config, plan, or runner changes during that pause. `apply.py` lines 790–817 recompute writes from live config; the inventory digest does not bind the approved preview.
findings.fix: Make approval specific to the previewed config rows and runner artifact action. Repeat the dry run immediately before applying; if its target, rows, or artifact actions differ, show the new preview and ask again. For a strict guarantee against a concurrent edit, have apply validate the approved preview fingerprint before writing.

findings.evidence: The routers-only case expects “Chooses router-backed models per tier without a scored catalog”; the supported routers-only scenario in `evals/02-opencode-routers-no-catalog.md` leaves missing tiers as `needs_choice`, and the JSON case supplies no inventory fixture to distinguish the two outcomes.
findings.fix: Give the JSON case a fixed unscored inventory with separate review and execution routers. Assert that the genuine router lanes remain available, unpopulated tier choices are shown without invented IDs, and no real apply runs while choices remain.

findings.evidence: There are eight positive and eight negative queries, but negatives such as “write a README for my personal dotfiles repository” and “explain how the Kubernetes horizontal pod autoscaler decides when to scale” do not test the skill's closest boundaries.
findings.fix: Replace several distant negatives with realistic near-misses: advanced GSD settings or integrations, dispatching or retrying an existing `cross-ai.mjs` lane, and reviewing a GSD plan without changing project configuration. Add an indirect positive that asks to give planning and execution different models without naming the curated skill.

findings.evidence: “On an offline or no-write request, do not run it … without it there is no fresh inventory to recommend from” covers the no-snapshot case but does not say where to resume when the user supplies an existing inventory, as the skill's own offline eval does.
findings.fix: Split that branch: if the user supplied a usable inventory for the target, continue at `recommend` without refreshing it, disclose that it is a snapshot, and respect any restrictions on scratch writes. If there is no usable snapshot, stop and ask before running inventory.

findings.evidence: “Merge `.new` by hand … check the active runner … then delete `.new`” does not give a pass criterion. The shipped runner can print `MISSING` or `NO MODEL` and still exit 0 in `--print-argv` mode (`skills/ai-kit-spec-review/references/cross-ai.mjs` lines 14904–14923).
findings.fix: Require the active template header and printed runtime, binary, model, and argv to match the approved selection. Treat `MISSING`, `NO MODEL`, and mismatched settings as failed validation; keep `.new` and report the discrepancy without dispatching a model.

findings.evidence: “pi sets `PI_PROVIDER` and `PI_MODEL` only” for the agent's own bash tool is version-sensitive, and the note gives neither an official source and checked date nor a live check of that distinction.
findings.fix: Link the official pi bash-tool implementation at a checked revision and date, or instruct the agent to verify which variable names are present from its own bash tool without printing their values. Preserve the `plan-unset` fallback.

findings.evidence: “Writes stay inside the project dir plus `/tmp` and `$TMPDIR`” is a concrete Codex sandbox guarantee. The runner can show which sandbox mode it requests, but that does not establish the installed version's effective writable roots.
findings.fix: Keep the v1/v2 permission distinction. Cite dated official Codex sandbox documentation for the stated roots, and distinguish the mode requested by the runner from the effective policy of the installed CLI.

findings.evidence: “The opencode bare profile is partial” names two directories that still load but does not source the current effect of disabling Claude skill discovery.
findings.fix: Cite dated official OpenCode documentation or source for skill search paths and the disable switch. Keep the warning that the profile does not isolate the runner from all installed skills.

findings.evidence: “`opencode run --standalone` (accepted by opencode v2.0.31)” gives a version and a claim about private versus shared service use without a dated source or a live help check.
findings.fix: Link the official OpenCode CLI reference with the date checked and point to `opencode run --help` on the installed version. Keep the separate caveat about the runner's model-listing call.

findings.evidence: “`--mcp-config <file> --strict-mcp-config` for claude and `--additional-mcp-config @<file>` for copilot” records version-sensitive vendor CLI forms without sourcing or a check at the point of use.
findings.fix: Have the agent check the installed runner's `--describe` for the generated form and its verification status, then confirm the form against installed vendor help or dated official documentation before relying on it for a review lane.
